title: Supervising physician eligibility, supervision and the written referral
rule_summary: Under 243 CMR 2.12(3)(a), to be eligible to participate in a collaborative drug therapy management agreement a physician must possess an active license to practice medicine issued by the Board AND must be ACTIVELY ENGAGED IN THE CLINICAL PRACTICE of medicine and the provision of patient care IN THE PARTICULAR FIELD of medicine in which the collaborative drug therapy management is to take place. Under 243 CMR 2.12(3)(b) the physician is the supervisor in the agreement and RETAINS THE ULTIMATE RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE CARE OF THE PATIENT, and in a community pharmacy setting a physician should enter into only as many agreements as he or she can reasonably and safely supervise at one time. Under 243 CMR 2.12(3)(c) the supervising physician SHALL ASSESS THE PATIENT AND MAKE A WRITTEN REFERRAL of the identified patient to the authorized pharmacist, and that written referral shall include a primary diagnosis and any co-morbid conditions that are included in the collaborative drug therapy management.
exam_relevance: Tests the positive side of physician eligibility, which turns on active clinical practice in the particular field as well as on an active licence, and the physician's assess-and-write duty, which 243 CMR 2.12(3)(c) states without limiting it to one practice setting.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Medicine regulations

common_confusions: An active medical licence alone does not make a physician eligible; the physician must also be actively engaged in the clinical practice of medicine and the provision of patient care in the particular field in which the collaborative practice is to take place.

243 CMR 2.12(3)(c) states the assess-and-write duty generally, while 243 CMR 2.12(1) defines Referral as a consultation outside the community pharmacy setting; the definition and the duty are separate provisions and satisfying the definition does not discharge the duty.
verification_notes: Read in the current official publication of 243 CMR 2.00 at the Board of Registration in Medicine download link on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule rather than by changing an existing record, so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
